DOLOR Ex-Officio Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member Sangguniang Kabataan Provincial Federation President Dear Sanggunian Members Marcos, Recto and Dolor: This refers to your letter dated 12 August 2025 requesting for this Department's formal guidance and intervention regarding the extent of their voting rights and privileges, particularly in the organization and reorganization of standing and special committees, as well as other positions within the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. At the outset it must be emphasized that Section 41 (b) of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160) expressly provides that the presidents of the provincial chapter of the Liga ng mga Barangay, the Philippine Councilors' League, and the Sangguniang Kabataan Federation shall serve as ex officio members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Their membership is by direct operation of law and not by appointment or election by the regular members. It is unequivocal that the Code does not make a distinction between regular and ex officio members in terms of rights and privileges. Both categories of members are treated as part of the same collegial body. Following the familiar rule in statutory construction, ubi lex non distinguit nec nos distinguere debemus (where the law does not distinguish, we must not distinguish), the voting rights of ex officio members stand on equal footing with those of regular members. The Supreme Court in Javier v. Cadiao, et all. definitively settled this matter, ruling that: "[Tlhe regular and ex officio SP members enjoy full rights of participation, which include debating and voting, all exercised in pursuit of championing the interests of their respective constituencies." G.R. No. 185369, 3 August 2016 "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

2025-07-31-055 page 2 Of 2 This categorical pronouncement leaves no doubt that ex offici0 members ot tne Sangguniang Panlalawigan enjoy the same voting rights as regular members, including in the adoption of internal rules, the election of officers, and the organization or reorganization of standing and special committees. Accordingly. any attempt to exclude ex officio members from voting in such matters would not only contravene the express provisions of the Local Government Coae out also run afoul of controlling jurisprudence. Such exclusion would unduly diminish the representational mandate vested in ex officio members and reduce their role to mere ceremonial participation, which is inconsistent with the law. In view of the law and jurisprudence, it is the considered opinion of this Department that. 1. Ex officio members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Oriental Mindoro are entitled to the full rights and privileges of membership, including the right to debate and vote on all matters brought before the body; 2. This entitlement necessarily extends to the organization and reorganization of standing and special committees, as well as the adoption of internal rules and the election of officers; and 3. Any action excluding ex officio members from voting in such matters would be contrary to the Local Govemment Code of 1991 and Supreme Court jurisprudence, and would therefore have no legal effect. We trust that the foregoing discussion sufficiently and comprehensively addresses your concems, and reaffirms the rights and privileges accorded to ex officio members under the law and jurisprudence. Rest assured that this Department remains steadfast in upholding the integrity of the legislative process at the provincial level. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY QF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P.
